study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Sex-specific normative age models estimated using quantile linear regression (50th/5th/95th percentiles) with 10-fold cross-validation.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used quantile linear regression to estimate the normative range (Allen et al. 2014; Jing et al. 2023; Lin et al. 2023).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Lin2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling for dynamic FC features

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Dynamic FC features derived from sliding-window FC matrices: average FC connection strength (aFCS) and fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (fFCS) across Yeo-17 networks (34 features).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The average FC connection strength (aFCS, mean of FC strength from all window-wise FC matrices) and fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (fFCS, average change of the windowwise FC strength) for each Yeo-17 network was yielded from time-varying dynamic FC matrices.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Normative models are age-based and estimated separately for female and male groups.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Based on the large public data set Cam-CAN, we estimated sexspecific normative age models for each dynamic FC feature.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Lin2024.pdf.md: Normative modeling for dynamic FC features
